her_coverage.summary: Core lane — she's a Mohs surgeon. 30+ videos; SCC example 737K (TT), BCC ultimate guide 493K (YT), and a fresh BCC 'advice as a skin cancer doctor' IG posted ~1 day ago.

themes.corpus_position: Skin cancer is extremely common — more than five million diagnosed each year. Basal cell carcinomas are the ones people mistake for dry skin or a pimple that won't heal: 'no amount of moisturizer is going to make it better.'

angles.angle: turn the quiz into a teaching series, not one-off guesses

themes.format_note: The pure guess-the-diagnosis quiz buys views but under-converts to follows (validated: quiz formats buy views, series/substantive education win follows). Run it as a numbered teaching series so the reach becomes followers.

her_coverage.summary: Deep, current: actinic keratosis treatment guide 439K (YT), 'reverse summer sun damage' 72K (TT), and a fresh IG on one blistering sunburn doubling melanoma risk (~3d).

themes.corpus_position: The precursor lesion to skin cancer is an actinic keratosis (AK) — skin cells that got mutations from sun exposure but haven't fully turned into cancer yet. Sun damage is cumulative; one blistering sunburn in youth can double your melanoma risk.

stitch_shortlist.author: @purascans
stitch_shortlist.claim: your lip balm is 'packed with' the same harmful ingredients

rubric.misses: 6.4d old — past the <4d rising window; 4.3M views make it worth catching anyway

pitch.the_claim: An 'ingredient safety scanner' account says the lip balm you reach for is packed with dangerous/irritating ingredients — 5,000+ comments of panic.
pitch.why_it_stitches: Specific fear claim, squarely in her lane, huge civilian audience, disproportionate comment heat (controversy signal).
pitch.your_fit: Directly grounded: her 2M lip-balm video says the real problem is IRRITATING ingredients — the tingling agents (menthol/camphor/fragrance) that make chapped lips worse. New angle: separate 'scary-sounding' from 'actually irritating.'
angles: empathy-first: the ingredient panic is understandable — here's what actually matters
switch-don't-quit: not 'throw it out' but 'read for tingling agents, not scary names'

stitch_shortlist.author: @skincarewithqm
stitch_shortlist.claim: exosome 'grow' brush serum for a healthier scalp & hair

rubric.misses: 6.1d old (slowing); exosome efficacy not in her corpus — grounded on FDA status + her scalp lane

pitch.the_claim: A 5.6M-view video sells an exosome 'grow' brush serum as the key to healthy scalp and hair.
pitch.why_it_stitches: Massive civilian wave in her UNDEREXPLOITED scalp/hair lane, and there is fresh news to peg it to (Dermatology Times exosome mythbuster, Aug 22).
pitch.your_fit: Needs her explicit take on exosomes, BUT she owns the scalp playbook (Malassezia/dandruff, minoxidil done right). Honest frame: 0 FDA-approved exosome products; OTC topical delivery through intact skin is thin/preclinical.
angles: 'you want me to WHAT?' — there are zero FDA-approved exosome products
what actually grows hair (minoxidil, done right) vs. what's marketing
yes-and: the biology is real; the serum claims run way ahead of it

pitch.the_claim: A 'comment REMOVE' account pushes an at-home skin-tag removal gadget — 1.66M views and still rising (3.4d).
pitch.why_it_stitches: Dangerous DIY claim, still climbing, in her exact lane — and 'is that even a skin tag?' is the perfect Mohs-surgeon hook.
pitch.your_fit: Her lane cold: the risk isn't the removal, it's removing something that isn't a skin tag (a BCC/melanoma can look like a 'tag'). Get it checked before you cut/freeze/burn it.
angles: the danger nobody mentions: what if it's not a skin tag?

news.headline: Moderna/Merck mRNA melanoma vaccine succeeds in Phase 3 trial
news.summary: Personalized mRNA vaccine + Keytruda cut melanoma recurrence vs Keytruda alone — first therapy of its kind to hit Phase 3; heading to regulators. Core skin-cancer news for a Mohs surgeon.
news.her_angle: a melanoma vaccine is huge — but early detection and sun protection still save lives right now
